paper.title: No Regrets for Learning the Prior in Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Meta-learning linear bandit with Gaussian rewards (hierarchical Gaussian prior)
unmapped: Sequential multi-task (meta-learning) setting: m tasks of n rounds each; task parameters theta_s ~ N(mu_*, Sigma_0) i.i.d., meta-parameter mu_* ~ N(mu_q, Sigma_q)
Learner knows meta-prior Q (mu_q, Sigma_q), task covariance Sigma_0 and noise sigma^2, but not mu_*
Regret is Bayes regret summed over all m tasks
settings.definition_quote: The learning agent interacts with $m$ instances, one at each of $m$ \emph{tasks}. At the beginning of task $s \in [m]$, an instance $\theta_{s, *} \in \Theta$ is sampled i.i.d.\ from a \emph{task prior} $P(\cdot; \mu_*)$ ... the reward distribution of arm $a$ is $p_a(\cdot; \theta) = \cN(\cdot; a\T \theta, \sigma^2)$ ... $P(\cdot; \mu) = \cN(\cdot; \mu, \Sigma_0)$ ... meta-prior $Q(\cdot) = \cN(\cdot; \mu_q, \Sigma_q)$

settings.name_in_paper: Meta-learning combinatorial semi-bandit with Gaussian rewards
unmapped: Sequential multi-task (meta-learning) setting: m tasks of n rounds; per-arm theta_s(k) ~ N(mu_*(k), sigma_{0,k}^2), mu_*(k) ~ N(mu_{q,k}, sigma_{q,k}^2)
Learner knows meta-prior and per-arm prior widths and noise, but not mu_*
Action set is a subset of all subsets of [K] of size at most L
settings.definition_quote: A \emph{stochastic combinatorial semi-bandit} ... is a $K$-armed bandit where at most $L \leq K$ arms are pulled in each round. After the arms are pulled, the agent observes their individual rewards and its reward is the sum of the individual rewards. ... the \emph{action set} is $\cA \subseteq \Pi_L(K)$

bound.expression_latex: R(m, n) \leq c_1 \sqrt{d m n} + (m + c_2) R_\delta(n; \mu_*) + c_3 d m,\quad R_\delta(n; \mu_*) \leq c_4 \sqrt{d n} + \sqrt{2 \delta \lambda_1(\Sigma_0)} n

symbols.n_rounds: number of rounds per task n
symbols.lam1_Sigma0: maximum eigenvalue of task prior covariance Sigma_0
symbols.eta: minimum eigenvalue of sum of forced-exploration arm outer products (Assumption a:forced explore)

conditions: there exist d arms a_1..a_d with lambda_d(sum a_i a_i^T) >= eta > 0
tuning: any delta in (0,1]; sublinear for delta = 1/n^2
forced exploration: pull a_1..a_d at the start of each task

source.label: thm:linearinfo
source.quote: The regret of \adats is bounded for any $\delta \in (0, 1]$ as R(m, n) \leq c_1 \sqrt{d m n} + (m + c_2) R_\delta(n; \mu_*) + c_3 d m, where c_1 = ..., c_2 = (1 + \sigma^2/(\eta \lambda_1(\Sigma_0))) \log m, and c_3 = 2 \sqrt{\|\mu_q\|_2^2 + \mathrm{tr}(\Sigma_q + \Sigma_0)}. The per-task regret is bounded as R_\delta(n; \mu_*) \leq c_4 \sqrt{d n} + \sqrt{2 \delta \lambda_1(\Sigma_0)} n

results.notes: Bayes regret summed over m tasks of n rounds each (total horizon mn). Here delta is a free tuning parameter of the analysis, not a failure probability. The per-task regret R_delta is substituted by its stated bound. The paper summarises the extra cost of unknown mu_* as O~(sqrt(dmn) + dm). The appendix proof has a forced-exploration term 2md sqrt(...), consistent with c_3 d m.

bound.expression_latex: R(m, n) \leq c_1 \sqrt{K L m n} + (m + c_2) R_\delta(n; \mu_*) + c_3 K^{3 / 2} m + c_4 \sigma \sqrt{2 \delta m} n,\quad R_\delta(n; \mu_*) \leq c_5 \sqrt{K L n} + \sqrt{2 \delta \tfrac{1}{K} \sum_{k} \sigma_{0, k}^2} n

symbols.n_rounds: number of rounds per task n
symbols.c_4: sqrt((1/K) sum_{k: sigma_{0,k}=0} log(1 + sigma_{q,k}^2 m/sigma^2))
symbols.c_5: 4 sqrt((1/K) sum_{k: sigma_{0,k}>0} sigma_{0,k}^2/log(1+sigma_{0,k}^2/sigma^2) log(4K/delta) log(1+sigma_{0,k}^2 n/sigma^2))

conditions: at most L base arms pulled per round (paper's L mapped to canonical m)
independent Gaussian per-arm rewards with diagonal prior covariances
tuning: any delta in (0,1]; sublinear for delta = 1/n^2
forced exploration: each arm pulled at least once per task (at most K rounds)

source.label: thm:semibanditinfo
source.quote: The regret of \adats is bounded for any $\delta \in (0, 1]$ as R(m, n) \leq c_1 \sqrt{K L m n} + (m + c_2) R_\delta(n; \mu_*) + c_3 K^{3 / 2} m + c_4 \sigma \sqrt{2 \delta m} n, where ... The per-task regret is bounded as R_\delta(n; \mu_*) \leq c_5 \sqrt{K L n} + \sqrt{2 \delta \tfrac{1}{K} \sum_{k \in [K]} \sigma_{0, k}^2} n

results.notes: Bayes regret over m tasks. The paper's L (max action size) is written as canonical m; the paper's m (tasks) is m_tasks. delta is a tuning parameter. The paper summarises: O~(sqrt(KLmn)) for learning mu_*, O~(K^{3/2} m) for forced exploration, O~(m sqrt(KLn)) per-task.
